previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and COPD, was admitted for hypoxia, somnolence, and cough productive of green sputum. She was found to have MRSA pneumonia and a suspected ESBL-producing Klebsiella urinary tract infection, leading to sepsis. She required ICU care for hypotension and hypoxia, managed with vasopressors, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and respiratory support. A central line was placed in the ED, later replaced with a PICC for outpatient antibiotic therapy. Her mental status fluctuated due to CO2 retention and over-sedation from home medications, prompting dose reductions in baclofen, pregabalin, and discontinuation of oxybutynin. She improved with treatment, was weaned to room air, and discharged home on IV Vancomycin and Ertapenem with nursing support.
problems: Methicillin resistant pneumonia due to Staphylococcus aureus
Urinary tract infection, site not specified

acute abnormality in the chest.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest were obtained. 
Evaluation is somewhat limited given underpenetrated technique and overlap of
arms on the lateral view.  There is stable mild cardiomegaly with apparent
pulmonary venous congestion.  There is a rounded opacity at the right lung
base which cannot be clearly seen on the lateral view.  The differential
includes atelectasis, mass, round pneumonia.  There is no large pleural
effusion.  No pneumothorax.  Right and left rib cage deformities are again
seen.  Hardware in the proximal humeri.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular congestion, rounded opacity at
the right lung base for which differential includes mass, pneumonia,
atelectasis.  Recommend followup to resolution.
